name: Flex / light industrial
summary: Small-bay flex (20k–100k SF, 18–24' clear, 2,500–10,000 SF bays) combines a light-industrial shell with 15–30% office/showroom finish, more storefront glazing, demising walls and a grade-level door per bay. Per-SF cost is well above bulk warehouse. No public benchmark isolates flex, so the default is built from Cushman & Wakefield's small-building shell figure plus a basic office finish allowance, cross-checked with RLB warehouse ranges — a derived estimate.

typicalSize.method: Typical multi-tenant flex buildings 20k–120k SF (judgment; smaller than C&W's 109k SF small distribution model).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: FAR ~0.28–0.41 (higher car parking than warehouse, smaller truck courts): 43,560 × 0.345 ≈ 15,000 SF/acre mid.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Flex zoning typically requires 1.5–4 spaces per 1,000 SF depending on office share (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Shell: C&W 2026 small-building average $144 psf at 109k SF (e1); flex buildings are smaller with more glazing and demising, offset by lighter yard → shell incl. sitework ≈ $140. Add office/showroom finish on ~20% of area at ≈ $90/SF (vertical-building block TI-basic mid $80, upgraded for storefront) = +$18 → mid ≈ $158, rounded $160. Low $115 ≈ RLB warehouse midpoints in Austin/Phoenix ($115/$128, e3/e6) — PEMB flex with 10–15% office. High $230 ≈ RLB national median-of-highs $228 (e2) and the top of Terrapin's mixed-use retail/industrial row ($225, e9). RSMeans 2019 small warehouse/factory ($108–$131 in 2019 $, e7/e8) escalate into the low-mid of this range.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P; shell, demising walls, grade-level doors, typical office/showroom finish (~20% of area), sitework, on-site utilities and parking. Excludes tenant-specific process utilities, racking, land, soft costs, off-sites and fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (115/160); premium ≈ high/mid (230/160 = 1.44) tempered to 1.3; luxury 1.55 for 2-story R&D/creative flex with heavy glazing and 40%+ office (judgment).

systemSplit.method: Warehouse split (C&W small-project shares: architectural ~22%, structure/enclosure ~34%; e10) adjusted for flex: more 08 storefront/grade doors, 09 office finishes, 22/23 restroom and office HVAC per bay; less truck-court paving. Judgment — verify.

lineItems.name: Office / showroom finish (~20% of area)

cost.method: Per SF of finished office: between vertical-building block tenant-improvement-basic ($45/$80/$120) and C&W 2026 office Gen-1 fit-out low markets (~$108, e23) / US average $162 (e20); flex office is a simpler spec than corporate office.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of baseline; raise the share for R&D/showroom flex.

cost.method: No public unit price fetched; insulated steel sectional door with operator, ramp/apron and bollards, judgment $4k–$10k. Roughly one per bay at 2,500–5,000 SF bays → ~0.0003 per SF.

Full-height (20–24 ft) metal-stud/gypsum or CMU demising wall ≈ $6–$13 per SF of wall × 20–24 ft height (judgment) ≈ $120–$320/LF. Quantity: one ~100 ft deep wall per bay; at an average demised bay of ~5,000 SF (50 × 100 ft) ≈ 100/5,000 = 0.02 LF per building SF.

pctOfHard.method: Higher than bulk warehouse (10–20%) because of smaller project size and multi-tenant design/permitting per bay; A/E ≈ 5–7% (RSMeans models carry 7%, e7) + permits/testing/insurance/developer overhead 7–15% (judgment).

design.method: Moderate design contingency for multi-tenant layouts (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $115 × 1.05; max ≈ hard high $230 × 1.35 (high-cost metro with full soft costs).

source.title: 2026 Americas Industrial Construction Cost Guide (landing page)

evidence.quote: Small projects averaged $144 psf (+3.6% YOY), medium $87 psf (+2.8% YOY), and large $78 psf (+2.3% YOY).
evidence.scopeNotes: Model 109,200-SF distribution building (size per CRE Daily); ground-up core and shell. Average of 46 Americas markets incl. Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, so not a pure US figure.

source.title: Industrial Construction Costs Rise Across Americas

evidence.quote: Structural and enclosure work was the biggest cost category … about 34% of a small warehouse budget … about 37% for a large project. Architectural work represented about 22% of costs on small projects and roughly 15% on large projects.
evidence.scopeNotes: C&W 2026 cost-category shares (structure/enclosure 34-37%, architectural 15-22%; the article also puts MEP near 6-7% across sizes); the remaining ~35-45% is not itemised in the article (presumably sitework and GC/fees).

openQuestions: No public flex-specific benchmark found; a published flex development budget (e.g., municipal incentive or REIT disclosure) would replace this derivation.
Office share varies widely (10–50%); the engine should expose it as an input.
